h1: The 7 Best Multi-Laptop USB-C Charging Stations for Desks and Classrooms, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 multi-laptop USB-C charging stations scored on total wattage, per-port power, port mix, build and portability.
summary: The Anker Prime 200W is the most proven multi-laptop station, with up to 100W per USB-C port from a compact GaN body. The Zobirez 750W is the one for several laptops that all need real power at once, the 380W dual 100W block suits a two-laptop desk, and the JOXPRING wheeled cart is the answer for a classroom or shared fleet.
intro: The headline wattage on a charging station is the least useful number on the box. A 500W label tells you what the whole unit can pull from the wall, not what a single laptop will receive when six other devices are plugged in. Many buyers end up with ten ports that happily trickle-charge phones and quietly starve their second laptop.

This ranking is built around that gap. We reviewed seven stations from their spec sheets and listings, looking at total wattage, power per USB-C port, port mix, build and form factor. Where a listing gives only a total with no per-port detail, we say that plainly, because it affects how many laptops the unit can really feed.

products.name: Anker Prime Charging Station, 200W 6-Port GaN Desktop Charger
products.verdict: A compact 200W GaN station that gives up to 100W per USB-C port.
products.description:
The Anker Prime is a 200W, 6-port GaN desktop charger that can deliver up to 100W from a USB-C port while several are in use. It measures about 4.4 by 3.0 by 1.4 inches, weighs 1.24 pounds and carries a 24-month warranty. It falls in the $50 to $100 bracket.

It leads because it pairs a brand with a long track record and a small, stable body. GaN, or gallium nitride, lets a charger run cooler and shrink compared with older silicon designs, which is why this one fits on a desk corner. The honest limit is the 200W total: two 100W laptops would use the whole budget, so a third device will force the power to be shared.

Buy it if you charge one or two laptops plus phones and want the most proven option. Skip it if you need four laptops at full speed.
pros: GaN keeps the body small and cool
products.idealFor: One or two laptops plus phones at a desk.
products.skipIf: You need to fast charge four laptops at once.

products.name: 750W Charging Station for Multiple Devices, Zobirez 10-Port Fast Charger
products.verdict: Five 120W USB-C ports and 750W total for a house full of laptops.
products.description:
The Zobirez has five USB-C ports at 120W each, five USB-A ports at 30W each, and a 750W total. It uses a one-piece ABS body with two wide bays for laptops or tablets and comes with a 10-cable kit. It sits in the $50 to $100 range.

It takes second place because it is the station that actually matches its marketing for multi-laptop families. Five 120W ports means several machines can draw serious power at once, and the cable kit saves a separate purchase. Compared with the Anker it is far bigger and has less of a premium feel, and ABS plastic does not shed heat like aluminum. Keep it in a ventilated spot.

Choose it for an office or a home with many laptops. Skip it if desk space is tight.
products.idealFor: Families and offices charging several laptops.
products.skipIf: You have little desk space or only one laptop.

products.name: 12 Ports Aluminum Alloy MEKIOJEO 380W Charging Station USB C Charger Block
products.verdict: Twelve ports in aluminum, with a dedicated 65W laptop port that holds speed under load.
products.description:
The MEKIOJEO offers 12 ports, eight USB-C and four USB-A, from a 380W total in an aluminum alloy body with GaN III and cooling protection. One dedicated 65W Power Delivery port is listed as staying at full speed when the others are busy. It falls in the $25 to $50 bracket.

Third place comes down to the dedicated laptop port, which is an unusually honest design: you know one machine will always get 65W. That suits a mixed household with one main laptop and many phones, tablets and earbuds. It does not suit several large laptops, since only one port has that guarantee. The aluminum case helps with heat and feels sturdier than plastic rivals.

Buy it if you have many small devices and one laptop to protect. Skip it if you need two or more 100W laptops.
pros: Strong value in the $25 to $50 bracket
products.idealFor: One laptop plus a pile of phones and tablets.
products.skipIf: You charge two or more power-hungry laptops.

products.name: 380W USB C Charger Block with 4 USB Cables Dual 100W Charging Station
products.verdict: Two confirmed 100W ports on a 380W block, with four cables included.
products.description:
This 380W charger block lists dual 100W ports and comes with four USB cables. It falls in the $25 to $50 bracket. The detail that matters is the pair of 100W ports, which is what two full-size laptops need to charge at normal speed together.

The unit lands fourth because the listing is short on other specs: we do not see a port count breakdown or a build description, so it is hard to compare with the MEKIOJEO. What it does promise is clear, and clear matters in this category. Two laptops at full speed from one block, plus cables thrown in, is a neat package for a shared desk.

Choose it if two laptops at 100W is the entire brief. Skip it if you want a long list of ports or cooling details.
products.skipIf: You need a long list of extra ports.

products.name: 510W Fast Charging Station for Multiple Devices, 10 Port USB C Charger Station
products.verdict: Ten USB-C ports on a 510W budget without paying for the top wattage tier.
products.description:
The 510W station lists ten USB-C ports and a total of 510W, all in the $25 to $50 bracket. It targets buyers who want the port count of a big station without moving up to the largest wattage tier.

Its fifth place reflects thin details. The listing does not state per-port wattage, so we cannot say how many laptops it would feed at full speed. Ten ports sharing 510W works out to an average of 51W, which is fine for phones and tablets and tight for several laptops at once. It sits between the MEKIOJEO and the Zobirez in capacity but offers less proof of how power is split.

Buy it if you want many USB-C ports on a modest budget. Skip it if you need guaranteed power per laptop.
pros: Ten USB-C ports in one unit
products.idealFor: Many USB-C devices on a modest budget.
products.skipIf: You need guaranteed power for each laptop.

products.name: Plugsharge 10-Device Laptop & Tablet Charging Station with 6 AC & 4 USB
products.verdict: Six AC outlets and four USB ports for homes that still own barrel-plug laptops.
products.description:
The Plugsharge station holds ten devices with six AC outlets and four USB ports, and it falls in the $100 to $200 bracket. The AC outlets are the point: they let you plug in the original adapters of laptops that do not charge over USB-C.

It ranks sixth because it solves a different problem from the rest of the list. If your laptops are older or are gaming machines with their own bricks, USB-C stations are useless to you, and a unit with AC outlets is the right tool. The cost is a higher price and less efficiency than a GaN USB-C design, because each laptop still carries its own bulky adapter.

Buy it if you mix AC and USB-C laptops. Skip it if everything you own charges over USB-C.
pros: Six AC outlets for original adapters
products.idealFor: Homes with a mix of AC and USB-C laptops.
products.skipIf: All your laptops already charge over USB-C.

products.name: JOXPRING Metal Laptop Charging Station with Wheels, 12 Device Mobile Charging Cart
products.verdict: A wheeled metal cart that stores and charges up to twelve devices.
products.description:
The JOXPRING is a metal charging cart on wheels with a capacity of 12 devices, priced from $50 to $100. It is built for storing and moving a group of laptops or tablets, rather than for sitting beside one desk.

It places last only because the job is specialized. A school, training room or small repair bench can roll it to where devices are needed and lock them away between uses, something a desktop block cannot do. The listing gives no wattage or port detail, so you should confirm what kind of charging it supports before depending on it for fast charging.

Buy it if you manage a shared fleet of devices. Skip it if you just want a charger on your desk.
pros: Stores devices as well as charging
products.skipIf: You only need a charger at one desk.

methodology.title: Total and per-port power
methodology.description: We weighed the total wattage against what each port can deliver, since a laptop cares about its own port, not the headline figure.

methodology.title: Port mix
methodology.description: USB-C, USB-A and AC outlet counts were compared against the devices a typical desk or classroom actually charges.

methodology.title: Build and heat
methodology.description: Aluminum bodies, GaN circuitry and warranty length were scored, because chargers that run hot age poorly.

methodology.title: Form factor
methodology.description: Size, weight and whether the unit sits on a desk or rolls on a cart decide where it fits.

methodology.title: Value and listing clarity
methodology.description: Price bracket against capability, with a penalty when a listing leaves out the wattage details that matter.

whatMatters.detail: The total is the most the station can draw, shared across every port. Per-port power is what each device can receive. A laptop needs roughly 65W to 100W, so a 200W total can only feed two of them. Read the listing for a per-port figure, not only the total.

Some stations reserve one port that keeps full power even when the others are busy. This matters when phones and tablets are plugged in alongside a laptop. Look for the phrase dedicated or confirmed in the listing, as vague claims often hide shared power.

Gallium nitride chargers run cooler and can be smaller than silicon ones at the same output. That helps desk space and longevity. Look for GaN in the listing, and check the warranty length as a sign of maker confidence.

USB-C handles modern laptops, tablets and phones, while USB-A suits older accessories, and AC outlets handle laptops with their own bricks. Count what you own before choosing. A station full of USB-A ports does little for laptops.

Aluminum conducts heat away better than plastic, which matters when several ports draw power at once. Poor cooling can throttle output. Look for aluminum or cooling mentions, and avoid burying the unit in a cabinet.

howToChoose.subheading: For a Classroom or Shared Office Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: High total wattage, multiple 100W-class ports or a storage cart, and a build robust enough for daily plug and unplug cycles. Cable management helps.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The JOXPRING cart suits storage and movement, and the Zobirez 750W offers the most real power for a busy room.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You charge several laptops simultaneously or want a known brand. The Anker Prime and Zobirez justify the step up.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You charge phones and one laptop. The MEKIOJEO covers that in the $25 to $50 bracket.

faq.q: Will these stations charge any laptop?
faq.a: Most USB-C laptops accept Power Delivery chargers, but some need more wattage than a port provides. Check your laptop's power requirement. Laptops that use a barrel plug need an AC outlet station such as the Plugsharge.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake buyers make?
faq.a: Trusting the total wattage. A 510W label does not mean each laptop gets a full share. Check the per-port power and any dedicated port.

faq.q: Is the Anker Prime worth it over a cheaper block?
faq.a: It is if you value a proven brand, a compact GaN body and a 24-month warranty. For many phones and tablets, cheaper stations offer more ports. Pick by how many laptops you charge.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Plug the station into a wall outlet, then connect each device with a cable rated for the wattage. Use the cables included where possible. A low-rated cable can limit laptop charging speed.
They warm up under heavy loads, and aluminum or GaN designs handle heat better. Leave space around the unit. Avoid covering it with papers or putting it inside a closed drawer.

faq.q: Can I leave a laptop charging overnight?
faq.a: Modern laptops manage their own battery charging, so it is generally fine. Use a quality unit and keep it ventilated. If a unit feels very hot, unplug it.

finalTake: The Anker Prime 200W is the safest pick for most desks, thanks to GaN efficiency, 100W ports and a proven brand. The Zobirez 750W is the answer for several laptops at once, and the MEKIOJEO is the budget route for one laptop plus many gadgets. For a shared fleet, the JOXPRING cart is the practical choice.
